RIGHT TO A COPY OF SIGNED EMPLOYMENT DOCUMENTS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS RIGHT-TO-A-COPY-OF-SIGNED-DOCUMENTS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes a California statutory right that can arise in connection with Acme, Inc.'s hiring and employment of Jordan Lee for the position of Software Engineer: the right of an employee or applicant who signs an instrument relating to obtaining or holding employment to receive a copy of that instrument. It summarizes selected requirements of California Labor Code section 432. It is not a determination that any specific instrument signed by Jordan Lee, any specific request made to Acme, Inc., or any specific copy furnished or withheld by Acme, Inc. in connection with the Software Engineer position complies or fails to comply with Section 432, and it does not itself make or satisfy a request, furnish a copy, or create any recordkeeping duty.

THE CORE RIGHT: ANY SIGNED INSTRUMENT RELATING TO OBTAINING OR HOLDING EMPLOYMENT
California law gives an employee or applicant who signs an instrument relating to obtaining or holding employment a right to receive a copy of that instrument. By its own text, the statute is not limited to a named category of document, such as an offer letter, an arbitration agreement, or a policy acknowledgment; it extends, on its face, to any instrument that an employee or applicant signs relating to the obtaining or holding of employment. The right belongs to "an employee or applicant" alike, so its text does not, on its face, distinguish between someone already on the payroll and someone who has not yet been hired.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "If an employee or applicant signs any instrument relating to the obtaining or holding of employment, he shall be given a copy of the instrument upon request."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 432 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, right to a copy of a signed employment-related instrument (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=432.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute (California Labor Code § 432), used as real evidence of California's copy-of-signed-instrument right — not a claim about which state's law governs any reader's situation. The section is a single, undivided sentence with no lettered or numbered subdivisions, so this citation and the citations in this information sheet's other authority clauses on Section 432 are drawn from that same one sentence; they are not independent corroborating sources of one another. The statute does not itself define "instrument" or state what makes a document "relating to the obtaining or holding of employment," and this clause does not resolve where that line falls for any particular document a particular employer uses. This clause is informational only: it does not itself determine that any specific document used by any particular employer is or is not an "instrument" within the meaning of Section 432, and does not determine that any particular employer's practices are compliant or noncompliant with it.

COMPLIANCE IS TRIGGERED BY A REQUEST, NOT MADE AUTOMATIC AT THE TIME OF SIGNING
By its own text, Section 432 conditions the duty to furnish a copy on a request: the statute provides that a signer "shall be given a copy of the instrument upon request." The statute's text does not state that a copy must be furnished automatically, without any request, at the time of signing. Its text also does not itself specify a deadline within which a copy must be furnished after a request is made, the form a request must take, whether it must be written or may be oral, or the person or office within an employer's organization to whom a request must be directed.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "he shall be given a copy of the instrument upon request."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 432 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, copy furnished upon request (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=432.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute (California Labor Code § 432), the same single, undivided sentence relied on in this information sheet's other authority clauses addressing Section 432; it is not an independent corroborating source. The reading that the duty is request-triggered rather than automatic rests on the plain "upon request" language quoted in this clause's citation; the statute does not separately use words like "automatically" or "at signing" in either direction, and this clause does not resolve how promptly "upon request" must be honored once a request is made. This clause is informational only: it does not itself determine that any specific request made or not made, or any specific copy furnished or withheld, by any particular employer toward any particular applicant or employee complied or failed to comply with Section 432.

WHAT SECTION 432'S TEXT DOES NOT SPECIFY — DEADLINE, METHOD, AND REMEDY
Section 432, in its own current text, does not specify a time limit within which an employer must furnish a requested copy, does not specify a required method or format for furnishing it, and does not itself state a penalty, civil remedy, or enforcement procedure for a failure to furnish a copy upon request. The section is a single, undivided provision, unlike some neighboring Labor Code sections on related hiring-document subjects that are broken into lettered or numbered subdivisions.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "If an employee or applicant signs any instrument relating to the obtaining or holding of employment, he shall be given a copy of the instrument upon request."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 432 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, full operative text confirming the absence of a deadline, method, or remedy provision (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=432.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute (California Labor Code § 432), used to document what its own text does and does not say — not a claim that no other law anywhere addresses timing, format, or remedy for a request of this kind, and not a claim about which state's law governs any reader's situation. This finding of statutory silence was reached by reading the section's complete current codified text, which is short enough to read in full, rather than a partial excerpt; the current codified version verified for this clause carries the annotation "(Amended by Stats. 1969, Ch. 714.)," confirming this is the section's current, unrepealed form as of the checked date, last amended in 1969. This clause does not identify any regulation, opinion letter, or reported court decision that fills these silences — an honest gap disclosed rather than resolved by assumption. A separate California statute, Labor Code section 1198.5, gives an employee or former employee a distinct right to inspect and receive copies of the employee's own personnel records and, unlike Section 432, does specify a response timeframe; this clause does not state that Section 432's copy-of-signed-instrument right and Section 1198.5's personnel-file-inspection right are the same right, that they share a timeframe, or that Section 432 incorporates Section 1198.5's timeframe by reference — nothing in Section 432's own text cross-references Section 1198.5. This clause is informational only and does not determine that any particular employer's practices are compliant or noncompliant with Section 432.

STATUTORY PLACEMENT AMONG THE LABOR CODE'S HIRING-DOCUMENT PROVISIONS
Section 432 appears in Article 3, "Contracts and Applications for Employment," a group of Labor Code sections numbered 430 through 435 addressing contracts and applications for employment. Other sections within that same numeric range address different subjects: Section 432.2 addresses polygraph, lie detector, and similar examinations required as a condition of employment; Section 432.5 addresses requiring an employee or applicant to agree in writing to a term or condition known to be prohibited by law; and Section 432.7 addresses inquiries into certain arrest, detention, and pretrial or posttrial diversion program history. None of those neighboring sections, in their own text, address an employee's or applicant's right to receive a copy of an instrument that employee or applicant has signed; within this article, that specific right appears in Section 432 alone.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "ARTICLE 3. Contracts and Applications for Employment [430 - 435]"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 432 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, Article 3 heading and section range covering Sections 430 through 435 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=432.)
  "No employer shall demand or require any applicant for employment or prospective employment or any employee to submit to or take a polygraph, lie detector or similar test or examination as a condition of employment or continued employment."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 432.2(a) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, polygraph and lie-detector examination prohibition (distinct subject) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=432.2.)
  "No employer, or agent, manager, superintendent, or officer thereof, shall require any employee or applicant for employment to agree, in writing, to any term or condition which is known by such employer, or agent, manager, superintendent, or officer thereof to be prohibited by law."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 432.5 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, prohibition on requiring agreement to an unlawful term or condition (distinct subject) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=432.5.)
  "An employer, whether a public agency or private individual or corporation, shall not ask an applicant for employment to disclose, through any written form or verbally, information concerning an arrest or detention that did not result in conviction, or information concerning a referral to, and participation in, any pretrial or posttrial diversion program, or concerning a conviction that has been judicially dismissed or ordered sealed pursuant to law, including, but not limited to, Sections 1203.4, 1203.4a, 1203.425, 1203.45, and 1210.1 of the Penal Code."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 432.7(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, restriction on inquiry into certain arrest, detention, and diversion-program history (distinct subject) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=432.7.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute and its immediate statutory neighbors (California Labor Code §§ 432, 432.2, 432.5, and 432.7, all within Article 3 of Chapter 3 of Part 1 of Division 2 of the Labor Code), used to document the current placement and boundaries of the copy-of-signed-instrument right — not a claim about which state's law governs any reader's situation. Sections 432.2, 432.5, and 432.7 are neighboring sections addressing distinct subjects, verified together for this clause to confirm none of them duplicates or restates Section 432's copy-of-signed-instrument right; they are not offered as independent corroborating sources for Section 432 itself, and this clause does not restate their substantive requirements beyond identifying their general subject matter. A section numbered 432.1 was checked directly against the California Legislative Information website, on two separate fetches using different browser identifications, and neither resolved to a codified section — the site returned its general search interface both times rather than section text — confirming there is currently no Labor Code section 432.1; this clause does not speculate about why that gap in the numbering exists. This clause does not determine that any particular employer's practices under Section 432.2, 432.5, or 432.7 are compliant or noncompliant with those sections; it is informational only.

REQUEST RECORD AND ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF RECEIPT OF SIGNED-DOCUMENT COPY INFORMATION
This acknowledges that Jordan Lee requested, in connection with employment with Acme, Inc., a copy of the following signed instrument(s) under California Labor Code section 432: Complete personnel file, including performance evaluations, and payroll records for the last three years of employment. Date of request: September 1, 2026. Delivery method: mailed to designated address.

Applicant/Employee: Jordan Lee
Signature: _______________  Date: _______________

On behalf of Acme, Inc.:
Signature: _______________  Date: _______________
